[{"role": "assistant", "parts": [{"type": "text", "content": "Here are some key facts on common design patterns for building LLM agents:

- **Prompt Chaining**: This pattern involves sequentially chaining prompts to guide the LLM through a series of tasks or decisions. ([Source](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents))
- **Routing**: LLMs can be directed to different processes or tools based on the context or input. ([Source](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents))
- **Parallelization**: Multiple processes or tasks can be executed simultaneously to improve efficiency. ([Source](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents))
- **Orchestrator-Workers**: An orchestrator manages and coordinates the actions of multiple workers, each performing specific tasks. ([Source](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents))
- **Evaluator-Optimizer**: This pattern involves evaluating the output of the LLM and optimizing the process based on the evaluation results. ([Source](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents))
- **Flows**: Event-driven workflows that give precise control over the interaction between LLMs and external systems. ([Source](https://docs.crewai.com/en/introduction))
- **Crews**: Teams of autonomous role-playing agents that can be orchestrated through Flows. ([Source](https://docs.crewai.com/en/introduction))
